internal_name: V8 (internal experiment name only; not a release version)
status: frozen before the parser was written and before any validation/test/probe record was scored by the parser
release_naming: V7/V8 are internal experiment names. The public release is gidi-finance-v2. If this experiment is validated, gidi-finance-v3 / 3.0.0 is only a CANDIDATE release name; nothing in this experiment confirms or ships v3.
question: Can the second neural value encoder (path B of gidi-finance-v2, V7) be replaced by a deterministic, rule-based value parser that runs on the unchanged gidi-finance-v1 type/target path, so that value quality is non-inferior to gidi-finance-v2 while model size, memory and latency drop?

in_scope: a pure-Python, deterministic, character-level value-span parser over the NFC text (src/gidi/value_parser/)
selecting one monetary amount among several numeric candidates by rules
returning the value as a substring span {text,start,end} in code points of the caller's original string, or null
measuring quality against gidi-finance-v2 INT8 with the frozen V7 scoring code, and cost (size, CPU latency, RSS)
out_of_scope: retraining, new/augmented/synthetic data, label changes, threshold or CRF changes on the v2 model
numeric normalisation (no number is derived from the span)
target extraction and anything under src/gidi/inference decoding: type and target come from the unchanged gidi-finance-v1 INT8 path

the production target error `mua sữa vinamilk hết 500k` -> `v` (resolved separately as an existing gidi-finance-v1 target-model error; recorded in tests/data/production-regressions.jsonl, prod-0001, and docs/deployment.md known limitations). No target code and no parser rule is changed for it
export, playground / web runtime port, release, publishing
a second parser attempt after held-out results
not_modified: the deployed site, Cloudflare, Hugging Face, GitHub releases

parser_design.approach: scan the NFC text character by character with an accent-folded, lowercased, length-preserving shadow string; build money candidates (number + unit + continuation + currency suffix); drop numbers explained by context as something other than money; choose one candidate by tier and position rules; map the span back to the caller's string with the inference NFC offset maps (gidi.inference.text.normalize_nfc)
money_forms: k; tr / triệu / trieu; củ / cu; xị / xi; chai; lít / lit (slang); ngàn / ngan / nghìn / nghin; tỷ / ty
currency suffixes đ / d / ₫ / vnd / đồng / dong
thousand-grouped numbers with . or , (80.000, 12,500,000), decimals (1,5tr, 2.3tr), plain digits (1500000), bare numbers (70, 100)
compound forms: 1tr5, 1tr150, 1 triệu 2, 3 củ 5, 1 ty 2, 2 củ rưỡi, 1 chai rưỡi, nửa củ
number words followed by a money unit: bốn triệu, hai trăm nghìn
competing_numbers_rejected_by_context: month / period / instalment / week / day / year numbers (tháng 10, t10, kỳ 3, đợt 2, lần 2, quý 4, năm 2023, mùng 3, thứ 6)
quantities followed by a classifier or measure (2 tô, 3 vé, 2 ly, 4 người, 10kg, 5 lít xăng, 2 chỉ vàng)
parser_design.selection: tiers: explicit money unit or money-shaped number (T1) > slang unit (T2) > bare number (T3); position rule within a tier is chosen on train only
parser_design.determinism: no randomness, no regular expressions on user text, linear scan, bounded look-ahead; the same text always gives the same span

development_rules: The parser is developed and optimised on datasets/annotation-v2/training-v1/train.jsonl ONLY (complete value labels; value_status == complete).
Reasonable optimisation = iterate on train errors with GENERAL rules (word lists, shape rules, tier/position rules). No per-string special cases, no memorised train texts, no note ids.

validation.jsonl, test.jsonl and probe-v1-eval-only.jsonl are evaluation-only. Their value labels and note texts are not read during development. Only aggregate facts were read before the freeze: row counts, value_status / value_provenance counts, and that test and probe share no id or text with train while 110 of the 149 validation rows are also in train (so full-validation numbers are optimistic; the 39 validation rows not in train are reported separately).

The rule-based proposer src/gidi/annotation/value_span.py that produced the rule-provenance labels is NOT imported by the parser and its source was not read for the design. It is used only as a labelled diagnostic baseline at evaluation time and for the category slices of the frozen scoring code (value_span_categories).

Development stops when the remaining train errors are ambiguous / label-noise cases or would need per-string rules. Parser source sha256 and the train dev numbers are then recorded in parser-freeze.json (written before any held-out scoring).

Held-out scoring runs ONCE with the frozen parser (scripts/run_value_parser_v8.py --stage heldout). The script refuses to run if parser-freeze.json does not match the parser source sha256 or if results already exist. No second attempt: if a bug is found afterwards it is reported, not tuned or fixed into the results.

validation.role: evaluation only; 110 rows are also in train, report the 39 not in train separately

test.role: evaluation only; the gated set (105 test-v1 + 38 test-targeted)

data.value_masking: metrics use value_status == complete only (uncertain value labels are masked), exactly as V7
data.circularity_risk: Most value labels (rule provenance, 807/889 complete train, 127/139 complete test, 76/81 probe) were produced by a deterministic rule proposer and accepted by stratum audit. A deterministic parser tuned on train labels can therefore agree with those labels because it imitates the proposer's conventions, not because it extracts amounts correctly. Mitigations: (a) human-provenance subsets are always reported separately and are the primary evidence; (b) the proposer itself is scored on the same sets as a diagnostic ceiling; (c) the parser was written without reading the proposer source; (d) pooled human held-out accuracy is a secondary acceptance condition. The human subsets are small (test n=12, probe n=5), so they cannot establish non-inferiority with statistical power; this is stated in the report.

baseline.name: gidi-finance-v2 INT8 (= V7 value-head seed 1 as shipped)
baseline.type_target_path: models/gidi-finance-v1 INT8 (sha256 a31caa5764c5ba99c44d4575da4695ce44232b836edb6d99b775558869dfc411), unchanged. gidi-finance-v2 path A is documented bit-identical to it; this experiment verifies type and target predictions of the two bundles are identical on every scored note

candidate_system: gidi-finance-v1 INT8 bundle (type + target, GidiPredictor, one thread) + value_parser.parse_value on the same caller string. No model file is changed.

scoring.code: frozen V7 scoring path reused, no new metric code: gidi.evaluation.value_metrics.evaluate_value, gidi.evaluation.value_eval.value_span_categories, gidi.evaluation.value_predict.prediction_rows, gidi.evaluation.value_gate.{summarize_set, seen_value_texts, value_quality_criteria, value_error_table, multi_number_errors}, scripts/compare_value_v1.load_sets, token offsets from the models/value-span-v7-dual-encoder/seed1 tokenizer (as scripts/score_web_parity_quality.py). Predictions come from GidiPredictor (caller-string offsets) and from the parser instead of from logits.
sets: validation (and its 39 rows not in train)
scoring.reported: value exact, span P/R/F1, token F1, present/null, human-provenance exact and rule-provenance exact, slices explicit_unit / bare_number / multi_number / slang / unaccented / unseen_span / long_multi_token / no_amount, error categories (value_error_category), every multi-number error, v8 vs v2 side by side, v8 vs proposer diagnostic
scoring.type_target: type accuracy / macro F1 / target F1 / exact from the v1 INT8 path and from v2 INT8; required identical

gating.G1_test_value_exact: test value exact (complete labels) >= 0.95  [frozen V7 criterion]
gating.G2_test_value_exact_human: test value exact on human-provenance labels >= 0.90  [frozen V7 criterion]
gating.G3_test_present_null: test value present/null accuracy >= 0.97  [frozen V7 criterion]
gating.G4_test_multi_number: multi_number test slice value exact >= 0.90  [frozen V7 criterion]
gating.G5_slice_floor: no value slice with n >= 5 on test below 0.80 exact  [frozen V7 criterion]
gating.G6_non_inferior_test_exact: v8 test value exact >= v2 test value exact - 0.02
gating.G7_non_inferior_present_null: v8 test present/null >= v2 test present/null - 0.01
gating.G8_non_inferior_human_exact: v8 test human value exact >= v2 test human value exact - 1 note (and G2)
gating.G9_non_inferior_multi_number: v8 test multi_number exact >= v2 test multi_number exact - 1 note (and G4)
gating.G10_type_target_unchanged: type and target predictions of the v1 INT8 path equal v2 INT8 on every note of validation, test and probe (0 differences)
gating.G11_cost_lower: candidate system (v1 INT8 bundle + parser source) is smaller than the v2 bundle, and its p50 CPU latency (one thread, same notes, same machine) is lower than v2 INT8's. Measured, not estimated.

secondary.S2_pooled_human_heldout_exact: value exact >= 0.90 on the pooled human-provenance complete rows of test, probe and the validation rows not in train
secondary.S3_no_crash_and_deterministic: parse_value never raises on any scored note or on the adversarial inputs of tests/test_value_parser.py and gives identical output on a repeat run

verdict_rule.ACCEPT_AS_V3_CANDIDATE: all gating criteria pass and S1-S3 pass. This means 'worth a follow-up validation as candidate gidi-finance-v3' only; it does not ship or confirm v3
verdict_rule.INCONCLUSIVE: all gating criteria pass but S1, S2 or S3 fails

acceptance_criteria.statistical_note: test has 139 complete values, 12 human, 22 multi_number, 0 no_amount; each note is 0.7% of test exact, 8.3% of human exact and 4.5% of multi_number exact. Non-inferiority margins are therefore declared in notes, not as significance tests.

cost_measurement.size: bytes on disk of models/gidi-finance-v1 and models/gidi-finance-v2 (model.int8.onnx and whole bundle directory) plus the parser source bytes; measured, not assumed
cost_measurement.latency: CPU, one onnxruntime intra-op thread, batch 1, GidiPredictor.predict on the 143 test + 81 probe notes, warm-up pass, 5 timed passes; p50/p95 per call for v2 INT8, v1 INT8 alone, parser alone, v1 INT8 + parser. Same process, same machine, interleaved order not required (each system timed in its own block)
cost_measurement.memory: peak and current resident set size (psutil / resource) in a fresh subprocess after loading the bundle and running the notes once, per system; the python+numpy+onnxruntime baseline is reported
cost_measurement.not_measured: browser / WebAssembly runtime: the parser is Python; a TypeScript port for the playground would be a separate piece of work and a parity risk, not costed here

known_limitations_declared_up_front: rule-provenance labels come from a rule proposer: circularity risk, see data.circularity_risk
no 'm' (2m = 2 million) money form unless train needs it; the deterministic parser cannot learn unseen spellings
multiple genuinely plausible amounts in one note are ambiguous by label (value_status uncertain) and are masked from the metrics
V8 does not address target extraction quality
artifacts: parser-freeze.json (parser source sha256, train dev numbers, written before held-out scoring)
